title: Q2 Nearest active incidents to an officer

compare.verdict: The optimized version asks the spatial index for the nearest candidates in distance order, instead of measuring every active incident and sorting them all.

rows.before: ORDER BY ST_Distance, which cannot use the spatial index
rows.after: ORDER BY the <-> operator, which can use a GiST nearest neighbour scan
Exact distance sort on 15 rows, keep 3

cases.label: Unoptimized
sql: ORDER BY ST_Distance(i.location, a.current_location) ASC, i.incident_id ASC

steps.title: Pick the officer
steps.text: Authority 1 supplies the reference point.

steps.title: Pair with every active incident
steps.text: The join has no spatial condition, so the officer is paired with all active incidents. Incidents 2 and 5 are resolved and dropped.

steps.title: Measure and sort everything
steps.text: ST_Distance is computed for every pair and the whole set is sorted. The index cannot help with this ordering.

steps.title: Keep three
steps.text: LIMIT 3 trims the sorted rows.

cases.label: Optimized
sql: ORDER BY ST_Distance(i.location, a.current_location) ASC, i.incident_id ASC

steps.title: Pick the officer
steps.text: Authority 1 supplies the reference point for the lateral subquery.

steps.title: Nearest candidates from the index
steps.text: The subquery walks the spatial index in distance order and stops after 15 rows. The sample has only 3 active incidents, so all 3 are returned.

steps.title: Exact re sort
steps.text: Exact distance is computed only for the candidates and they are sorted precisely.

steps.title: Keep three
steps.text: LIMIT 3 returns the closest incidents.

LEFT JOIN incident i ON i.zone_id = z.zone_id

steps.title: Join every incident
steps.text: Each zone is joined to its incident rows. Zone 1 gets 3 rows and zone 2 gets 2, so 5 joined rows exist.

sql: DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(zic.total_incidents, 0) DESC) AS risk_rank
LEFT JOIN zone_incident_counts zic ON zic.zone_id = z.zone_id
ORDER BY risk_rank ASC, z.zone_id ASC;

steps.title: Count incidents per zone
steps.text: Incident is scanned once and grouped by zone_id. 5 rows become 2 summary rows.

steps.title: Join the summary
steps.text: Zones are joined to 2 summary rows instead of 5 incident rows. A zone with no incidents would still appear.

steps.title: Rank
steps.text: DENSE_RANK works on a plain column, so no group is needed after the join.
